name: Fortop Referral Search Term
author: fortop

sections.description:
Fortop Referral Search Term is a modernization inspired by SEO SearchTerms Tagging 2 version 1.535 by Purwedi Kurniawan (poer), maintained by fortop. It is not an official successor, transfer of the original listing, or claim of endorsement.

This release supports local referral analysis and relevant, reviewed visitor navigation. Do not use it for keyword stuffing, doorway/search-page generation, artificial link building, or ranking manipulation. Moderation does not make irrelevant keyword lists appropriate. No indexing, ranking, or traffic improvements are promised.

Licensing: GPLv2 or later. The original directory snapshot has no explicit license header. The official Plugin Directory requirements state that code without a specified license is considered GPLv2 or later: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/ . This is the documented basis, not a newly obtained personal license grant or transfer of the original listing. The full GPLv2 text is included in LICENSE.txt; the header permits later versions. No original screenshots, third-party images, or bundled libraries are included in this installable package.

Features:

  • Optional local collection of search terms actually disclosed in referral URLs.
  • Administrator moderation before terms can be displayed publicly.
  • Post-specific, popular, recent, random, and category term lists.
  • A modern multi-instance widget and [stt2_terms] shortcode.
  • Public legacy template-function compatibility for common STT2 theme calls.
  • Explicit, batched import from the original table without changing it.
  • Explicit addition of an approved term as a post tag by an authorized administrator.
  • Configurable retention, prepared database statements, capability and nonce checks, and escaped output.

Collection and automatic content append are OFF on a new installation. All collected and imported terms are pending review. This is intentionally not a drop-in reproduction of every legacy behavior.

The plugin makes no external HTTP requests. It stores a term, destination post ID, aggregate count, last-seen UTC time, moderation state, and a hash of the term. It does not store IP addresses, full referral URLs, cookies, or visitor identifiers. The hash is for deduplication, not anonymization. Terms themselves can contain personal information. Administrators must update their privacy notice and assess applicable consent requirements before enabling collection. Requests with Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, and logged-in visitors, are excluded.

Daily cleanup deletes terms in the new table after the configured last-seen retention (90 days by default), including approved/imported terms. Expired terms are excluded from public lists even before cron runs. The original table is never modified or deleted. Deactivation and plugin deletion preserve data; remove sensitive terms while the plugin is active and use your database tools for a complete, backed-up removal if required.

Credits

Original project: SEO SearchTerms Tagging 2 v1.535 by Purwedi Kurniawan (poer), Copyright 2010-2011. Original category-query credit: pile. The new implementation is a development candidate prepared for maintainer fortop. No original-author endorsement is implied. Official original source: https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/searchterms-tagging-2/trunk/ . License interpretation follows the Plugin Directory requirements linked above; this does not transfer ownership of the old listing.
sections.installation:
1. Create a staging copy and back up the database and original plugin.
  2. Deactivate the original SEO SearchTerms Tagging 2, the previous SEO Referral Search Term package, and any earlier Referral Search Terms beta on that staging site. Saved data is retained.
  3. Upload this candidate ZIP and activate it on the individual site. Network activation is intentionally not supported.
  4. Open Settings > Fortop Referral Search Term. Review retention/privacy and optionally import legacy rows, 100 per click.
  5. Review and approve only suitable terms. Add the Search Terms widget or shortcode and check your theme.
  6. Enable collection or automatic append only when you deliberately want those behaviors.

Do not activate the old plugin while this candidate is active. Deactivate this candidate first when rolling back. Re-enable the original plugin to use its unchanged original table/settings.
sections.faq:
How do I upgrade from the earlier SEO Referral Search Term candidate?

Back up first, deactivate and delete the earlier candidate, then install and activate this package. Do not run both packages at once. Existing stt2m settings, terms, approval state, import cursor, widget placements and shortcodes are retained; only the package name, directory and text domain change. Existing translations for the former text domain must be regenerated for fortop-referral-search-term. Deleting either inactive package preserves the stored data. The new plugin restores a missing daily cleanup schedule on the next request if removal of an older package cleared the shared hook.

Does this plugin show promotions or dashboard-wide notices?

No promotions, upgrade prompts, rating requests or dashboard widgets are included. Conflict notices appear only on the Plugins screen or this plugin’s settings screen for administrators with plugin-activation capability. They are dismissible for the current page view and remain available there while the conflict is unresolved. Action feedback is confined to the plugin settings screen.

Can this recover hidden Google search queries?

No. Search engines and browsers commonly omit search terms from referral headers. No terms can be recovered when they are absent. This is not Search Console and does not guarantee SEO or traffic improvements. Full-page caching may bypass collection.

What are the collection limits?

The table has an approximate 50,000-row ceiling, terms are limited to 255 characters, and capture uses a soft global 60-per-minute throttle. Concurrent requests can exceed these non-atomic limits. Deduplication ignores ASCII letter case but preserves Unicode case consistently across hosts. Only standard public posts/pages are supported; third-party membership access rules and cached-page purging need separate integration.

Are referral counts trustworthy analytics?

No. Referrer headers can be forged. Counts are observations without visitor identification, not unique people or proof of search-engine traffic. The soft global throttle is not a firewall.

What is supported by the shortcode?

[stt2_terms mode=”post” limit=”10″ link_mode=”none”]
Modes: post, popular, recent, random, category. Optional post_id, category_id, heading, and link_mode (none, post, search). Only approved terms for public non-password-protected posts/pages or the home page are displayed. Random chooses from a bounded popular pool rather than the entire table.

Which theme functions remain?

stt_terms_list(), stt_popular_terms($count), stt_recent_terms($count), stt_random_terms($count), and stt_popular_terms_in_category($count). They return HTML; echo the returned string in the theme. Internal pk_stt2_* APIs and old widget IDs are not preserved.

Does import preserve the original data?

Yes. Import only reads the original stt2_meta table and writes a separate stt2m_terms table. It sanitizes terms, skips unsupported/private/missing destinations and blocked phrases, clamps invalid/future dates, and uses idempotent maximum-count updates. It does not copy old options or widget placements. Imported terms are pending and subject to current retention; old imports can therefore be immediately hidden/cleaned. Keep the original backup.

What changed from the legacy plugin?

The old newsletter/registration/donation integrations are removed. Automatic publication-date changes are not implemented. Automatic tagging is replaced with an explicit administrator action for an approved term. Raw custom HTML wrappers and rewrite/search-query rewriting are removed. The installation instructions and feature differences above describe the migration requirements.

Is this ready for WordPress.org?

Version 0.1.1 is prepared for submission review, not an approved directory release. The final requested name is Fortop Referral Search Term and the intended slug is fortop-referral-search-term. Pending/reserved slug availability and acceptance can only be determined by the directory. A new fork does not inherit the existing listing or its rights. Local review of each Plugin Check warning does not guarantee directory approval. Final package verification and an authorized submission are still required.

What has been tested, and what is outside the verified scope?

Revision 0.1.1 (November 14, 2026) passed 149 assertions per matrix on WordPress 7.1.4/PHP 8.3.36, WordPress 7.1.4/PHP 8.4.27 and WordPress 6.5.14/PHP 7.4.33 in Playground with SQLite compatibility. Coverage includes syntax, activation, capture/privacy, moderation, storage limits, pagination, restricted/dismissible notices, prior-package guards and cleanup schedule restoration. Debug logs were empty. An additional old-0.1.0-to-new-0.1.1 upgrade scenario passed eight assertions covering retained terms/settings/import cursor/widget data, shortcode and cleanup recovery. Plugin Check 2.2.0 executed all 36 checks with zero errors/warnings; the previously documented narrowly scoped exceptions remain in place. These are automated tests, not WordPress.org approval. Native MariaDB and browser layout testing have not been rerun for 0.1.1.

Historical evidence for the earlier release follows, not a claim of new native testing:
Release 0.1.0 passed 136 assertions on each of WordPress 7.1.4/PHP 8.3.36, WordPress 7.1.4/PHP 8.4.27, and WordPress 6.5.14/PHP 7.4.33 using Playground with SQLite compatibility, without PHP errors or debug-log output. All 36 Plugin Check 2.2.0 checks ran: the annotated release reported zero errors/warnings; an independent control without the new exact-line exceptions reported the original 32 warnings. These are reviewed exceptions, not 32 bug fixes. PHP token comparison against beta.4 found only the version constant changed.

The beta.4 baseline also passed 67 native staging assertions on WordPress 7.1.4/PHP 8.3.36/MariaDB 10.11.19, a separate persistent synthetic import and fresh-process verification (26 and 19 assertions with overlapping coverage), a small six-increment concurrency check, and responsive browser previews with Twenty Twenty-Five.

The installed 0.1.0 release then passed a native persistent-import check on the same stack: 2 precondition assertions, 41 run assertions, and 19 fresh-process verification assertions, all with exit code zero and no errors in their logs. These stages overlap and are not a sum of unique cases. Actual import batches processed 100 rows, then 9, then an empty batch; the persistent cursor was 109. Original source rows were preserved. The existing importer intentionally renormalized one synthetic future-date fixture when reimported; this was verified, not treated as byte-unchanged target data. Anonymous staging checks showed the approved demo term and excluded pending batch terms. All eight installed plugin files matched the tested package before this documentation-only update; PHP files remain unchanged. These results are not a certification of every supported version or host.

Only standard public, non-password-protected posts/pages and the home page are supported. Network activation is not supported. Native MySQL, other native PHP versions, production migrations, high-load races, FlexMag/other production themes, AMP, physical mobile devices, third-party membership restrictions, and page/persistent-object-cache integrations remain unverified. Full-page caches can bypass collection and retain old public output after moderation or visibility changes; the site operator must arrange cache purging. No term-result cache is added by this plugin. Stage-test the actual deployment before production use.
sections.changelog:
0.1.1

  • Renamed to Fortop Referral Search Term with the fortop-referral-search-term slug and text domain.
  • Limited conflict notices to the Plugins and plugin settings screens for users who can activate plugins. Notices are dismissible; moderation/import feedback remains on the plugin settings screen only.
  • Added automatic restoration of a missing shared cleanup schedule after removal of an earlier package.
  • Added a load-order-safe guard against the previous SEO Referral Search Term package. Storage keys, tables, import cursor, widget ID and shortcode remain unchanged.

0.1.0

  • Prepared the initial release for submission review; directory approval is not claimed.
  • Documented all 32 Plugin Check warnings with exact-line exceptions for custom validation, prepared custom-table operations, fresh-state reads/writes, and five guarded legacy template aliases. These are reviewed exceptions, not 32 bug fixes.
  • Updated verified testing scope and remaining deployment limitations without changing collection, storage, moderation, import, display, or data-preservation behavior.

0.1.0-beta.4

  • Avoid duplicate Settings API notices on the standard WordPress Settings screen; keep moderation/import notices unchanged.

0.1.0-beta.3

  • Development modifications dated November 10, 2026; modification notices retained in source headers.
  • Use the unique term/post index before counting rows, so repeat captures/reimports avoid a full-table count.
  • Use one look-ahead row for admin pagination instead of a total-count query.
  • Fail closed when a storage admission query errors.
  • Saturate hit counts with a conditional expression that avoids an overflowing intermediate on SQLite compatibility runtimes.
  • Keep moderation, retention, visibility, and capacity queries fresh; no cross-request term cache was added.

0.1.0-beta.2

  • Adopted the final maintainer-selected name Fortop Referral Search Term and matching text domain.
  • Added the GPLv2-or-later license declaration and full license text based on the official directory fallback rule.
  • Clarified appropriate navigation/analysis use and prohibited keyword-stuffing/ranking-manipulation use.
  • Kept original attribution and excluded historical screenshots from the installable package.
  • Guarded against class collisions with the earlier private beta after the slug change.

0.1.0-beta.1

  • Reimplemented local collection, storage, display, moderation, import, and widgets using modern WordPress APIs.
  • Added explicit privacy-safe defaults, strict host/parameter checks, prepared SQL, escaped output, and capability/nonces.
  • Preserved original data; provided public template compatibility and manual tagging.
  • Added bounded random queries, retention filtering, strict date validation, and future-date clamping.
  • Removed external registration, automatic tagging/republication, legacy rewrites, and arbitrary HTML wrappers.
